objective.text: Understand area as the amount of flat space a shape takes up. Area is measured in square units.

explanations.title: What is area
explanations.text: The amount of flat space a shape takes up is called its area. Shapes can look different and still have the same area.

explanations.title: Cover a shape with no gaps
explanations.text: To measure area, cover the shape with same-size blocks. The blocks must not leave gaps. They must not overlap. They must not go outside the sides.

explanations.title: Block size and block count
explanations.text: The bigger the block, the fewer blocks you need to cover the same shape. A trapezoid covers more area than a triangle.

explanations.title: Square units
explanations.text: When we cover a shape with squares, the units are square units. A rectangle covered by 6 squares has an area of 6 square units.

examples.title: Shape A and Shape B
examples.text: It takes 6 triangles to cover Shape A. It takes 6 triangles to cover Shape B. The triangles are all the same size. So the two shapes have the same area.

examples.title: Trapezoids cannot cover the rectangle
examples.text: Trapezoids cannot cover the rectangle without gaps, overlaps or going outside the sides. Squares can. So we use square units to measure its area.

objective.text: Find all whole number side lengths of rectangles with an area of 24, 36, 48 or 72. Move the parentheses and use the associative property.

explanations.title: Move the parentheses
explanations.text: Write one side length as a product. 3 times 12 is 3 times (2 times 6). Move the parentheses: (3 times 2) times 6 is 6 times 6. This gives new side lengths with the same area.

explanations.title: Switch the order
explanations.text: Use the commutative property. Switch the factors in the parentheses to find more side lengths. (2 times 3) times 6 becomes 2 times (3 times 6), so the sides are 2 and 18.

explanations.title: Check all the numbers
explanations.text: To find all whole number side lengths, check each number from 1 up. 1 is always a side length. Numbers that do not multiply by a whole number to make the area are not side lengths.
